items.title: 3 Legacy Financial Dividend Stocks That Never Go Out of Style
items.summary: A bank founded as a water company in 1799, a Newark insurer and a Wall Street giant all promise retirees rising income. Two of them quietly slashed payouts in the financial crisis, and one never flinched. Which one?

items.title: What If the Fed Doubles the Rate Hike in December? These 5 Dividend Stocks Could Prosper
items.summary: Markets say a quarter-point hike is nearly certain, but a hot inflation print could change that fast. Five dividend payers, from banks to an oil giant to a toothpaste maker, each win in a different way if the Fed gets aggressive.

items.title: 5 High-Yield Dividend Stocks That Can Actually Afford Their Payouts
items.summary: With Treasuries paying more than 5.2%, a dividend needs real cash behind it to justify the risk. We checked the coverage on five payers across insurance, energy, malls, snacks, and private credit, and one of them barely clears the bar.

items.title: Can Multiple Employer Solutions Boost VOYA's Retirement Business?
items.summary: Voya Financial's MES assets nearly double to $200 billion, while surging PEP adoption and expanded retirement solutions could unlock new growth opportunities.

items.title: MTG Q3 Earnings Beat on Lower Expenses, Revenues Fall Y/Y
items.summary: MGIC beats Q3 earnings estimates as insurance-in-force growth and expense discipline help offset rising losses and delinquencies.

items.title: Aflac Just Extended Its Dividend Growth Streak to 44 Years. Is It a Buy?
items.summary: Aflac posted a quarter that missed estimates for the fourth time in a row, yet the dividend sailed on untouched. Behind the ugly headline sits a payout cushion and one overseas risk that income investors cannot ignore.
